A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MeCo by the same authors, despite the revised title. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original MeCo evaluations on E.T.Bench, Charades-STA, and QVHighlights, alongside controlled comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: V2 retains original MeCo evaluations and adds results for a QWen2VL implementation, dataset-wise fine-tuning, loss variants, and failure cases.

M1.justification: The structural-token, query-focused-captioning, and contrastive-grounding framework remains intact. V2 Appendix B introduces a dataset-wise fine-tuning adaptation: one final transition token represents all background frames, replacing temporally interleaved transition tokens in that setting. MeCo is also implemented on QWen2VL-7B.

E1.justification: The datasets and nine E.T.Bench tasks are retained. However, v1 Table 2 and Section 5.3 evaluate standalone QVHighlights multi-segment moment retrieval; v2 drops that evaluation and retains highlight detection. Added dataset-wise fine-tuning uses existing datasets rather than expanding task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands the reported comparator set. Table 1 adds Dispider, Tarsier, Tarsier2, and QWen2-VL; Table 2 adds Seq2Time, NumPro-FT, VideoChat-T, and specialist comparisons including M-DETR, UMT, QD-DETR, CG-DETR, and UniVTG. Table 7 adds the Interleaving strategy. Its Positional Embedding rows match v1's Timestamp Tokens rows and are not a new comparator.

E3.justification: V2 adds dataset-wise fine-tuning on Charades-STA and QVHighlights, a QWen2VL-7B configuration, and Charades-STA R@1 at IoU 0.3. These extend the evaluation design beyond v1's zero-shot comparisons. The highlight metric label changes from HIT@0.1 to HIT@1, but shared values remain identical, so an underlying recalculation is not established.

E4.justification: V2 Table 6 newly quantifies asymmetric versus symmetric grounding losses and frame-level versus segment-pooled features. Table 7 extends QFC compatibility testing to Interleaving. Appendix F and Figure 6 add four failure cases concerning incorrect attention, boundaries, event counts, and transition prediction. V1's existing component and backbone ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and averages across tasks. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Shared MeCo ETChat results remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial result entries. For example, MeCo QWen2VL reports Charades-STA R@1 0.5 of 50.1 zero-shot and 68.5 after dataset-wise fine-tuning, plus fine-tuned QVHighlights mAP of 45.3. These concern new configurations or protocols, not improvements under unchanged settings. V1's QVHighlights moment-retrieval mAP results, including MeCo's 26.2 and 27.4, are removed.

T1.justification: V1 Section 4.1 explicitly requires consecutive segments to tile the video; v2 removes those constraints and explicitly admits overlapping events in Figure 3 and Appendix E. V2 also defines segment-pooled features for the added loss variants. The central language-model and grounding equations remain equivalent, and no formal proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central claim that semantic structural tokens and query-focused captions improve temporal localization is retained. V2's conclusion extends the effectiveness claim to dataset-wise fine-tuning, beyond v1's zero-shot evidence. Its introduction also drops v1's explicit claim to be the first framework eliminating all generated boundary-related information.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the brief account of unstable symmetric-loss training with an explanation based on fewer negative samples. Section 6 introduces a substantive tradeoff between semantic generalization and precise boundary modeling, explicitly declining to replace boundary-centric approaches entirely. Appendix B discusses temporal-position biases, while Appendix F identifies specific failure mechanisms absent from v1's general acknowledgment of room for improvement.

D1.justification: V2 adds stage-specific freezing details, hidden-state layer choices, overlap handling, QWen2VL integration instructions, and a statement describing supplementary code and generated data. The original hyperparameter table, hardware, and prompt templates are retained. Some specificity is lost: Table 1 omits per-model frame counts and numerical LoRA ranks, and Appendix D drops v1's explicit rank/alpha exception.

R1.justification: V2 substantially refreshes the literature coverage, adding newer temporal methods such as Chrono, LLaVA-MR, and VideoChat-T, specialist comparisons, and additional contrastive-learning foundations. It removes v1's cognitive event-segmentation, visual-attention, and background-modeling literature. The semantic-versus-boundary positioning remains, but the supporting research context and explicit novelty framing are revised.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. V1's separate Preliminary section is absorbed into Method; captioning precedes grounding; training and inference receive a dedicated subsection. V2 also reorganizes the appendices and adds separate limitations, reproducibility, acknowledgments, and manuscript-assistance disclosures.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column to a single-column layout. Figures 1–2 are redrawn, new label-construction and failure-case figures are added, and Tables 1–2 are substantially restructured. Colored result highlighting becomes bold/italic emphasis. The inference algorithm moves to the appendix, while existing qualitative examples and prompt figures are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical support and the account of applicability. The loss ablation quantifies a previously underexplained design choice; newer comparators, another backbone, and dataset-wise fine-tuning test broader practical validity. Specific failure cases and the boundary-precision limitation make the conclusions better qualified. These gains outweigh the loss of standalone QVHighlights moment-retrieval evidence and some baseline-setting detail.
